subject: Dedicated capacity: GPU allocation escalation and proposed prioritization
messages:
From: Rebecca Lin <rebecca@NimbusHealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example>
Cc: Elaine Yuan <elaine.yuan@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2026-02-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity timeline + risk (GO-LIVE 3/15)

Marissa —

Thanks again for the walkthrough today. Quick note from our side: we’re targeting a hard go-live for the AI-assisted triage feature on 2026-03-15. Our security/compliance signoff is done but our infra team flagged potential contention risk if other large customers are scheduled onto the same Dedicated GPU pool in early March.

I attached an updated forecast with expected RPS and peak concurrent sessions (NBH_forecast_v2.xlsx). Can you confirm:
- whether Redwood will guarantee capacity for a 6-week canary window (3/15–4/26)
- what preemption or QoS policies might apply if capacity gets tight

We’re evaluating two contractors that will run inference through the dedicated endpoint — low tolerance for cold preemption. If we can’t get a firm commitment by next Tuesday (3/2), our product team may delay the launch.

— Rebecca
VP, Platform Engineering
Nimbus Health
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example>

Date: 2026-02-28T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity timeline + risk (GO-LIVE 3/15)

Rebecca —

Appreciate the clarity and the forecast spreadsheet. I’ve looped in Dev (solutions) and Hannah (infrastructure ops) to map constraints to action. Short answers up front: we can *scope* a 6-week canary, but final commitment depends on available reserved capacity and any high-priority commitments already in the queue.

Proposed next steps:
- Internal alignment today on current Dedicated pool reservations and any pending allocations that could conflict.
- Quick call tomorrow (2/29) 10:00 PT with Dev + Hannah to walk the forecast and discuss preemption/QoS options.
- I’ll send a written allocation proposal by EOD 3/2 that itemizes guaranteed v. best-effort capacity and suggested mitigations.

Can you confirm the canary SLO (p95 latency target) and whether you need single-tenant GPUs (no noisy neighbors)?

— Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.example>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.example>
Cc: Rebecca Lin <rebecca@NimbusHealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity timeline + risk (GO-LIVE 3/15)

Marissa / team —

Thanks for the context. Short technical summary after an infra review:
- Current Dedicated GPU cluster (us-west-2) is ~82% committed for March 2026. There are two near-term reserved requests: AcmeFinance (deal ACME-2026-005) requesting sustained capacity for a 3/1 start, and a renewal for Acme that would add ~16% additional reserved load.
- With the pipeline as-is, if both Acme and Nimbus attempt to cutover in early March, we’ll exceed the conservative provisioning threshold and risk elevated queuing and KV cache thrashing — this would particularly impact models with long-context behaviour (your triage LLM).

Options to avoid service impact:
1) Reserved burst (short-term rented GPUs for 4–6 weeks) — fastest but costlier; we can price + capacity in the allocation proposal.
2) QoS tiers with soft preemption — guarantees baseline tokens/s but allows reclaim for higher-tier customers. Requires customer buy-in (preemption policy + notice window).
3) Canary scheduling — stagger cutovers (e.g., Nimbus 3/15, Acme 3/22) and enforce strict warm start window to minimize cold starts.
4) Single-tenant nodes — we can place Nimbus on isolated hardware if available; this is the strongest isolation but capacity-limited.

I’ve attached a rough allocation matrix we can refine (allocation_matrix_v1.xlsx).

Recommend we run option (3) + (1) as fallback if capacity delta > 12%. If leadership wants to prioritize Nimbus over Acme, we need that prioritization decision in writing by 3/2 so we can enforce scheduling.

— Dev
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.example>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.example>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.example>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.example>
Date: 2026-03-02T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Allocation decision required — Nimbus vs Acme prioritization

Team —

Internal note (do not forward externally): after reconciling committed reservations and pending pipeline, the practical choices are narrow. High-level impact:
- If we approve Acme’s immediate start (scheduled 3/01), we will be forced to: 
  * shift Nimbus to best-effort with throttled burst (higher risk of degraded p95 latency) OR
  * spin temporary on-demand nodes (~12–16 GPUs) at extra cost.
- If we prioritize Nimbus for a guaranteed canary, we must delay or negotiate Acme’s start to 3/22+; Acme is a sizable ARR but not yet contracted on a long-term reserved capacity product (they requested short-term reserved).

Prioritization criteria I propose:
1) Contractual commitments (reserved monthly commits > 6 months)
2) Regulatory / compliance needs (air-gapped on-prem customers get top priority)
3) Launch criticality (hard product go-live windows with regulatory risk)
4) Strategic relationship / expansion potential (existing expansion + referenceability)

Under these criteria, Nimbus (hard go-live 3/15 with HIPAA scope) should be prioritized unless Sales prefers otherwise. If Sales wants Acme prioritized, we will require a cross-charged on-demand buffer to avoid impacting Nimbus.

Requesting written confirmation from Sales/Revenue leadership by EOD 3/02. Jonas — please confirm whether the temporary on-demand pool can be provisioned within 24 hours and estimated cost.

— Hannah
Head of Infrastructure Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity timeline + risk (GO-LIVE 3/15)

Rebecca —

Quick external update after internal alignment: we recognize the 3/15 go-live priority and Hannah’s infra assessment. Proposed path forward (we want your sign-off):

1) Guaranteed 6-week canary on dedicated endpoint with targeted p95 SLA 250ms for the baseline workload you supplied — contingent on a signed addendum to your order for a short-term Reserved Burst (6 weeks). Pricing and exact GPU count are in the attached allocation matrix.

2) Canary start 3/15 with a warm window (3/15–3/17) where we’ll run a controlled ramp to validate KV cache and pre-warmed runtimes. If the ramp shows >12% unexpected load, we will trigger a temporary on-demand pool; costs for that fallback are covered by the Reserved Burst addendum.

3) We will not preempt active inference requests during the canary window unless there is a catastrophic capacity event; instead we’ll throttle new sessions and notify you with 15m advance where possible.

If you approve, please:
- Reply ACK to this thread by 3/04 and we’ll circulate the addendum and DocuSign link.
- Confirm the p95 target and any additional compliance constraints.

Thanks — we want to avoid any last-minute delays and are aligned on minimizing user impact.

Best,
Marissa Cole
